p.8 可以看到 §6 从底部约 70% 位置开始。p.9 上半部分是 Table 2 + §6 剩余文本（"Diagnostic value beyond aggregate calibration" + "Implications and future work"），Limitations 从 p.9 约 55% 位置开始。

§6 仍然有约 15-20 行溢到 p.9。需要再压缩约半页内容。Table 2 浮动到 p.9 顶部是关键原因——如果 Table 能留在 p.8 或者 §5.5 文本更短，§6 就能压入 p.8。

最有效的方式：进一步压缩 §5.4 和 §5.5，让 §6 + Table 2 都落在 p.8 内。

57	\subsection{Exploratory Domain Analysis}
58	\label{sec:domain_differential}
59	
60	\begin{figure}[t]
61	\centering
62	\includegraphics[width=\columnwidth]{figures/fig_domain_gamma.pdf}
63	\caption{Per-domain $\gamma_d$ estimates with 95\% CIs ($J$=13 Qwen2.5). STEM domains show positive $\gamma_d$ while Humanities and Social Sciences are negative. At $J$=16, Social Sciences $P(\gamma_d\!<\!0) = 99.7\%$ survives Bonferroni correction (\S\ref{sec:domain_differential}). These patterns are family-specific (\S\ref{sec:cross_family_validation}).}
64	\label{fig:domain_gamma}
65	\end{figure}
66	
67	\paragraph{Within-family directional heterogeneity.}
68	Figure~\ref{fig:domain_gamma} ($J=13$) and Table~\ref{tab:domain_gamma} (Appendix~\ref{sec:domain_gamma_table}) present per-domain $\gamma_d$ estimates for Qwen2.5 (0.5B excluded per \S\ref{sec:injection}). At $J=16$, STEM domains show positive $\gamma_d$ while Social Sciences is negative. Social Sciences shows the strongest directional signal ($\gamma_d = -0.63$, 95\% CI $[-1.07, -0.19]$, posterior $P(\gamma_d\!<\!0) = 99.7\%$, PPP$=$0.722), crossing the Bonferroni-corrected threshold of 99.375\% for eight independent tests. This is a suggestive finding that requires higher-powered replication with $J \geq 50$ models. Prior sensitivity analysis confirms this signal is data-dominated rather than prior-dominated ($\hat{\gamma}_d$ varies only 1.2$\times$ across priors vs.\ 2.6$\times$ for the pooled estimate; Appendix~\ref{sec:prior_sensitivity}). ARC-Challenge model fit is marginal across all tested configurations (PPP $< 0.05$ at $J=8$, 13, and 16), which prevents reliable domain-level $\gamma_d$ estimation on this benchmark. The pooled MMLU estimate ($\gamma_{\text{pooled}} = +0.11$, CI $[-0.40, +0.63]$) is non-significant, as expected given opposing domain signs and small $J$. These directional patterns are family-specific: cross-family pooling shifts domain-level $\gamma_d$ estimates, and the STEM-positive pattern observed within Qwen does not generalize across families (\S\ref{sec:cross_family_validation}).
69	
70	Dose-response analysis (Figure~\ref{fig:dose_response}) shows scale-dependent effects: at 1.5B and 3B, accuracy increases with dosage, while at 0.5B, accuracy \textit{decreases} (0.41 $\to$ 0.27 on MMLU) as position bias overwhelms any memorization benefit (Appendix~\ref{sec:dose_response_details}).
71	
72	\subsection{Cross-Family Exploratory Analysis}
73	\label{sec:cross_family_validation}
74	
75	\paragraph{Calibration generalizes; diagnosis does not.}
76	To test whether these properties extend beyond a single architecture, we pool Qwen2.5 and Llama-3.2-3B in a single IRT run (concurrent calibration, placing all $\theta_j$ on a common scale; d000 models serve as anchors; Table~\ref{tab:cross_family}). Calibrated MAE remains below 0.02 on every benchmark (MMLU 0.008, GSM8K 0.008, ARC 0.015), which confirms that IRT ability estimation generalizes across model families. All three $\gamma$ estimates are non-significant, with CIs spanning zero. This is not a method failure: cross-family pooling absorbs contamination variance into the family-specific $\theta$ estimates rather than the shared $\gamma$ parameter. PPP values indicate acceptable benchmark-level fit (MMLU 0.60, GSM8K 0.83, ARC 0.45), but per-domain fit degrades substantially in cross-family pools, which confirms that $\gamma$ diagnosis requires family-stratified analysis.
77	
78	\paragraph{$\theta$ asymmetry across families.}
79	GSM8K reveals that families respond to contamination through $\theta$ rather than $\gamma$: Qwen2.5-3B shows $\Delta\theta = +0.57$ from d000 to d100, while Llama-3.2-3B shows $\Delta\theta \approx +0.05$. IRT absorbs this differential response into family-specific $\theta$ trajectories, which maintains calibration without an identifiable shared $\gamma$.
80	
81	\begin{table}[t]
